fullPassage: [P01] For astronauts in space, the force of gravity is weaker than it is on Earth. Because of this, astronauts sometimes develop symptoms of "space sickness," such as headaches, nausea, and vomiting. Space sickness is related to the small organs deep inside our ears that detect information about the movement of the body. They send this information to the brain, and the brain uses this information to keep the body balanced. In the low gravity of space, the information sent by those organs changes. According to scientists, this difference confuses the brain and results in the symptoms associated with space sickness. Luckily, space sickness does not last very long. After a few days, the brain adapts to the lower gravity of the astronauts' environment, and the symptoms go away. However, in some cases, astronauts can experience "gravity sickness," which has symptoms that are similar to those of space sickness, when they return to Earth. [P02] The sixteenth century Spanish novel The Adventures of Esplandian, written by Garci Rodriguez de Montalvo, describes an island paradise east of Asia called California. It is believed that this novel was the first place the word "California" appeared in print. The novel is also thought to be where the areas called California in modern-day Mexico and the United States got their names. The Adventures of Esplandian was very popular when the Spanish were exploring Mexico, and the legend of California was widely known. It seems that when Fortun Ximenez and Hernan Cortes first sailed north along the western coast, they mistook what is now called the Baja California peninsula for the fictional island and named it California. It took many years to correct the misguided belief that the peninsula was an island. By that time, California had already been well established as the name for both the peninsula and the land to its north that is now the US state. [P03] People often complain about foreign aid being sent to other countries. They claim that the money is wasted, and sometimes this is true. However, this mostly happened in the past, during a time when aid was given to persuade countries to become allies. Today, most foreign aid is used to improve people's lives, so the problem has become much smaller. Reducing the amount of foreign aid that is wasted is a worthwhile goal. But even more importantly, we should be teaching people the reality behind the myth of what happens to foreign aid. The money actually goes toward improving the health of people living in poverty and making their communities better places. As a result, we have the opportunity to live in a world where no one needlessly suffers simply because of where they were born. [P04] All living things suffer during water shortages. Yet some animals, particularly those in places with dry seasons, have amazing adaptations that help them survive dry conditions. Two such animals, the Galapagos tortoise and the desert tortoise, save up water in their bladders. Drinking water from rainfall and green plants allows them to fill their bladders. The tortoises can then survive on the stored water throughout the dry period. Other dry-climate animals have adaptations that allow them to keep water in. For example, a special kind of toad in North America called the desert spadefoot spends 75 percent of its time deep under the ground. There, it wraps itself with a sticky temporary skin that keeps water from escaping. When the seasonal rains arrive, the spadefoot comes out again. [P05] Most people think of the imagination as something internal and private, and it is true that one can imagine something without anyone else knowing about it. But even this purely mental projection has its source in the outside world and the social community that we are a part of. Without drawing on material that exists beyond our selves, no mental image could ever come into being. This means that, while we might believe that our imagination is ours alone, the ingredients that it draws upon are in fact shared by many others. Some might consider this a limitation, but the social quality of imagination actually makes it possible for society to come together around shared values. In fact, the concept of morality depends on this. When we share the same basis for considering possible actions, we are able to make fair judgments about what is right and wrong and formulate social standards that every member of a community can agree upon. [P06] When an ant happens to come upon a new source of food, the colony quickly reorganizes itself to harvest from it without any orders from a colony leader. This can be done because the ant leaves a trail of pheromones as it follows the scent of the new food source. This new trail is noticed by another nearby ant, which then alters its own path. It won't be long before its change in direction is noticed by a different ant, and so on. After the new information quickly spreads throughout the entire colony, every ant has now adjusted itself to gather from the newly discovered food source. No conscious decision is being made by any individual ant to alter the colony's behavior. Nevertheless, a new behavioral pattern emerges for the benefit of the colony.

det.korean: 더 약한 — 혼란시키다 — 적응하다

questions.passage: [P01] For astronauts in space, the force of gravity is weaker than it is on Earth. Because of this, astronauts sometimes develop symptoms of "space sickness," such as headaches, nausea, and vomiting. Space sickness is related to the small organs deep inside our ears that detect information about the movement of the body. They send this information to the brain, and the brain uses this information to keep the body balanced. In the low gravity of space, the information sent by those organs changes. According to scientists, this difference confuses the brain and results in the symptoms associated with space sickness. Luckily, space sickness does not last very long. After a few days, the brain adapts to the lower gravity of the astronauts' environment, and the symptoms go away. However, in some cases, astronauts can experience "gravity sickness," which has symptoms that are similar to those of space sickness, when they return to Earth. [P02] The sixteenth century Spanish novel The Adventures of Esplandian, written by Garci Rodriguez de Montalvo, describes an island paradise east of Asia called California. It is believed that this novel was the first place the word "California" appeared in print. The novel is also thought to be where the areas called California in modern-day Mexico and the United States got their names. The Adventures of Esplandian was very popular when the Spanish were exploring Mexico, and the legend of California was widely known. It seems that when Fortun Ximenez and Hernan Cortes first sailed north along the western coast, they mistook what is now called the Baja California peninsula for the fictional island and named it California. It took many years to correct the misguided belief that the peninsula was an island. By that time, California had already been well established as the name for both the peninsula and the land to its north that is now the US state. [P03] People often complain about foreign aid being sent to other countries. They claim that the money is wasted, and sometimes this is true. However, this mostly happened in the past, during a time when aid was given to persuade countries to become allies. Today, most foreign aid is used to improve people's lives, so the problem has become much smaller. Reducing the amount of foreign aid that is wasted is a worthwhile goal. But even more importantly, we should be teaching people __________ of what happens to foreign aid. The money actually goes toward improving the health of people living in poverty and making their communities better places. As a result, we have the opportunity to live in a world where no one needlessly suffers simply because of where they were born. [P04] All living things suffer during water shortages. Yet some animals, particularly those in places with dry seasons, have amazing adaptations that help them survive dry conditions. Two such animals, the Galapagos tortoise and the desert tortoise, save up water in their bladders. Drinking water from rainfall and green plants allows them to fill their bladders. The tortoises can then survive on the stored water throughout the dry period. Other dry-climate animals have adaptations that allow them to keep water in. For example, a special kind of toad in North America called the desert spadefoot spends 75 percent of its time deep under the ground. There, it wraps itself with a sticky temporary skin that keeps water from escaping. When the seasonal rains arrive, the spadefoot comes out again. [P05] Most people think of the imagination as something internal and private, and it is true that one can imagine something without anyone else knowing about it. But even this purely mental projection has its source in the outside world and the social community that we are a part of. Without drawing on material that exists beyond our selves, no mental image could ever come into being. This means that, while we might believe that our imagination is ours alone, the ingredients that it draws upon are in fact shared by many others. Some might consider this a limitation, but the social quality of imagination actually makes it possible for society to come together around shared values. In fact, the concept of morality depends on this. When we share the same basis for considering possible actions, we are able to make fair judgments about what is right and wrong and formulate social standards that every member of a community can agree upon. [P06] When an ant happens to come upon a new source of food, the colony quickly reorganizes itself to harvest from it without any orders from a colony leader. This can be done because the ant leaves a trail of pheromones as it follows the scent of the new food source. This new trail is noticed by another nearby ant, which then alters its own path. It won't be long before its change in direction is noticed by a different ant, and so on. After the new information quickly spreads throughout the entire colony, every ant has now adjusted itself to gather from the newly discovered food source. No conscious decision is being made by any individual ant to alter the colony's behavior. Nevertheless, a new behavioral pattern emerges for the benefit of the colony.

❌ ③ the history of international relations(국제 관계의 역사)는 본문의 요점이 역사가 아닌 현재 원조의 실제 효과라는 점에서 부적절
✅ ④ the reality behind the myth(통념 뒤에 숨은 현실)는 외국 원조에 대한 잘못된 믿음(myth) 뒤의 현실(reality)을 가르쳐야 한다는 원문에 정확히 맞는다 ←정답
det.tip: the reality behind the myth = 미신/통념 뒤에 숨은 현실. myth = 근거 없는 통념. 외국 원조가 낭비된다는 통념 뒤의 현실을 알려야 한다.

❌ ③ created by individual effort(개인의 노력에 의해 만들어진)는 상상력의 재료가 외부에서 온다는 본문과 모순

det.tip: shared by many others = 다른 많은 사람들이 공유하는. 상상력의 재료(ingredients)는 외부 세계에서 왔기에 사실상 공유된다는 역설.
